entries.16.39: Then, drenched with streams of blood for water, like a well-flowered ashoka tree risen upon a mountain, the son of Vasava came senseless to the ground in the fight, like the fallen banner of Indra.
entries.17.53: Having spoken thus, his mouth parched and himself stricken by the stroke of the arrow, that great-souled son of the vanara king gazed upon Rama, who resembled the sun, and remained silent.
entries.20.14.1: "Kakutstha feels no remorse, having slain Vali out of place while he was fighting with another, and having done a deed most reprehensible."
entries.20.26: So Tara of blameless hue, weeping piteously beside her lord with the vanara women, resolved to fast unto death and to sit down there on the ground where Vali lay.
entries.22.32: Then Tara, plunged in an ocean of calamity, gazed upon the face of her dead lord, and embracing Vali sank to the ground, as a creeper clings to a great tree that has been felled.
entries.25.53: Then, having set alight that Vali of foremost manhood, of might equal to blazing fire, slain by the shaft of the best of the Ikshvakus, the vanara approached Rama along with Lakshmana.
entries.26.42: Then the valorous lord of the vanara host, having announced the great consecration to the great-souled Rama and regained his wife Ruma, obtained the kingdom as the lord of the thirty gods obtains his.
entries.33.66: Of the hue of finest gold and large-eyed, the hero seated upon a noble throne embraced Ruma closely, and beheld Saumitri of undaunted spirit, large-eyed as himself.
entries.40.34.1: "The rivers rising from the mountains with their many fearsome recesses are to be searched, and the mountains full of caverns, and the woods."
entries.42.56: "When the wife of the lord of men of measureless splendour has been found, we shall have accomplished our purpose by requiting what was done for us."
entries.42.57: "Whatever else beyond this is to be done, and may be conducive to this task, is to be determined by your honours as suits the place, the time and the purpose."
entries.42.58: Then all those monkeys headed by Sushena, having heard the shrewd word of Sugriva, took leave of the lord of monkeys and went to that quarter which is guarded by Varuna.
entries.45.16: Then the vanaras there, proud of their strength, spoke thus one after another in the presence of the king of vanaras.
entries.48.24: Having searched again and grown weary, they came forth and met together, and sat down dejected in a solitary place at the foot of a tree.
entries.57.20: "My father, along with his counsellors, was shut out by Sugriva; and Rama, having slain Vali, consecrated him."
entries.57.21: "Thus employed by Rama and searching here and there, we do not find Vaidehi, any more than one finds the light of the sun by night."
entries.57.22: "With full care we searched the Dandaka forest, and unknowing entered an open cavern of the earth."
entries.57.23: "We are all doers of the word of the king of monkeys; having overpassed the term appointed us, we have taken to a fast unto death out of fear."
entries.57.24: "When Kakutstha and Sugriva and Lakshmana are enraged, there is no life for any of us even if we go there."
entries.65.35: Then the foremost hero of the vanaras urged on Hanuman himself, that renowned best of those who leap, who had taken a place apart and was seated at ease.
entries.66.38: Then, urged by the bull among monkeys, that monkey of proven speed, the son of the wind, gladdening the host of vanara heroes, made his own form huge.
